# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s146) | **THE DEPLOY — develop `632f16dfe` live on the Secuura demo, 31/31 images, 33 containers healthy, residue MEASURED at 3** (2026-09-07 15:50, on Kam's 13:40 word lifting Wednesday's hold) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **VERIFIED BY ARTEFACT WITH A NEGATIVE CONTROL, which is what makes the verification a measurement rather than a list.** Each of the five merges confirmed by a content marker in the DEPLOYED image — and then **its own UNMERGED KS-952 work (`dist/rateLimitScope.js`) checked and found ABSENT**, so the markers discriminate between what shipped and what did not instead of everything answering PRESENT. Anchoring booted `cardanoMode: "REAL (Blockfrost)"` — the runbook's mandatory post-redeploy check, run rather than assumed. **KAM'S IDENTITY, the four-part statement delivered exactly as constrained: 10 files BEFORE → 3 AFTER**, all three host-side `dist/` output the rsync excludes by design, **with the control that makes it mean something — the fictional identity 0 files → 7** — and measured **INSIDE the running container** (auth: fictional 1x, real address 0x), not merely on disk. **It did not blur the half that did not happen:** the `…060` row is unchanged, and it carried the staging consequence forward — fix KS-962 and the row rewrites itself on the next boot. **🔴 IT CAUSED A SIDE EFFECT, DETECTED IT, REVERTED IT, AND REFUSED TO 'FIX' IT.** `up -d` created a default-profile `demo-service` that entered a restart loop. **It PROVED the pre-deploy state rather than assuming** (`DEMO_SERVICE_ENABLED` absent from the VM `.env`, 0 matching lines; `.env` mtime unchanged at 09-03; `guardian`/`queue` showing `Up 22 hours`, which a restart loop cannot show), stopped it to restore that state — **and deliberately did NOT set the flag, because that service mints real Platform Admin tokens with no caller credential.** *"An explicit security opt-in, and enabling it on a public demo is Kam's call, not a seat's fix for its own restart loop."* **Flagging rather than fixing, on the one thing where fixing was easiest.** **Across the whole 2-hour build it also: front-loaded its handover at 50% on instruction; built a three-class waker after catching that its first could only observe SUCCESS; caught its own orphaned background task BY DURATION; refused to invent a ticket id for an artefact Wednesday had referred to as existing; corrected Wednesday's own §4 ("his address is untouched") with a measurement; and found the prune trap that justified the disk bound better than Wednesday's reasoning did.** **Housekeeping clean: `.env` never sent and verified untouched · nothing deleted at any point · guard v2 never fired · 8.2G free · 0 build failures.** |
| Secuura/Blockchain-B (board execution seat, s148-B) | **Executing the catalogue under Kam's 13:40 judgement grant — cancelled Wednesday's restructure before it moved, held 6 of 17 archives, delivered the hierarchy enumeration** (2026-09-07 14:01, CLOSED) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **IT KILLED WEDNESDAY'S PROPOSAL BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING, on a measurement neither of us had.** Linear allows ONE PARENT PER ISSUE and KS-763/KS-778 already sat under **KS-771, a review stream** — so instrument parents and review-stream parents compete for the same slot, and the fold would have **removed tickets from the stream Peter reviews through**, undoing a shape Kam adopted as *"the process going forward"*. **It established its own SEAT IDENTITY by measurement first** — two briefs 64 seconds apart to different seats, settled on Wednesday's own sentence *"ahead of KS-952"* naming another seat's
